themes.title: General – Power / Grid Equipment & Energy Transition

hero.oneLiner: The deck positions Diamond Power Infrastructure (DICABS) as an integrated manufacturer of power transmission equipment and turnkey services operating India's largest single-location cables and conductors complex at Vadodara, riding a capex-led grid, renewables and data-centre demand cycle with large capacity headroom.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Described as "India's largest single-location cables & conductors complex" — a 110-acre integrated campus at Vadodara, Gujarat, with 2.8 mn sq ft constructed and 55 acres available for expansion.
- Vertically integrated: billets to wire rods to conductors to cables, all in-house ("wire-rod → conductors → cables"), which the deck frames as stronger control over the value chain.
- Founded 1970 with 55+ years in operation; 665 clients including marquee industry names, and 132 type tests recognised in leading labs (elsewhere stated as 145 type tests).
- Licensed manufacturing partner of TS Conductor, USA for Aluminium-Encapsulated Carbon-Fibre Core (AECC), positioned for the grid-modernisation and HTLS re-conductoring super-cycle.
- Reference projects cited include Khavda Solar Park (Adani), Mundra Port, Delhi International Airport, NTPC, GETCO, SAIL, ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India, Tata Power Renewable Energy (302.4 MW Bijapur-KA wind) and a Hyderabad data centre built by L&T, Sterling & Wilson and Blue Star.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- A ₹1,614 Cr QIP was completed with allotment of 7.11 Cr shares on 28-Jul-2026, taking the share count to 59.81 Cr equity shares.
- Project A is to be funded from QIP proceeds and accruals with no term debt; working capital of ≈₹428 Cr at 90% utilisation and peak funds ≈₹558 Cr are to be funded within the QIP working-capital pool.
- Post-QIP shareholding: promoter and promoter group 74.03% (within the 75% cap, MPS achieved), institutions 14.24%, public float 15.53 Cr shares (25.97%), 66,795 shareholders, zero promoter pledge with no encumbrance or lock-in, and 99.99% of shares in demat.
- Marquee institutional holders named: Motilal Oswal MF (3.43%), HDFC MF (2.21%) and Smallcap World Fund - Capital Group (1.21%).
- FY26 net fixed asset turnover of 1.4x versus 0.9x in FY25, framed alongside the capacity-utilisation ramp.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Alliance] Licensed manufacturing partnership with TS Conductor, USA for AECC; the product is type-tested at Kinectrics lab and the company participated in tenders worth ₹1,200 Cr, including ₹500 Cr with PGCIL.
- [Exports/Certification] 145 type tests completed, NABL-accredited 700 kV UHV lab and BIS certification, with a BASEC / CPR / UL roadmap for Europe, USA, Middle East and Africa under process (NABL Phase-1 audit of the in-house lab completed) to open export order inflow.
- [Industry outlook] Roadshow data cited: India cables & wires market ₹350 bn (FY14) to ₹900 bn (FY25) to ₹1,467 bn (FY29E) with a ~10 to 13% CAGR; organised market share 57% (FY14) to 80% (FY27E); transmission investment ₹3 Tn (FY22-26) to ₹5 Tn (FY27-31P); power-sector investment ₹37-42 Tn over FY27-31P.
- [Demand drivers] Data-centre capacity 350 MW (FY19) to 1,300 MW (FY25) to 5,000 MW (FY30P); RE generation investment ₹12 Tn (FY22-26) to ₹30 Tn (FY27-31P); railway electrification 68% (FY20) to 93% (FY24); Green Energy Corridor of ~9,700 ckm and 22,600 MVA across eight RE-rich states.
- [Ambition] Project A is described as "one of the volume engine of the ₹4,000 → ₹7,500 Cr revenue ramp".
